title: Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is specified for Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw because its 900+ MPa tensile strength allows thin-wall tube shaping without buckling, critical for lightweight frame and component structures. The alpha-beta microstructure delivers 45% higher specific strength than 4140 chromoly steel, translating directly to gram-level weight savings where it matters. Its high-cycle fatigue endurance limit (>500 MPa @10^7 cycles) matches the pedaling load spectrum of Shoe cleat fixing screw set. This rationale is driven by shoe cleat fixing screw set and fat life requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for pedal hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g with SPC sampling
Go/No-Go ring gauging with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for shoe cleat fixing application
commonFailures: Fatigue failure at head tube junction - mitigated by smooth weld radius >=5mm + post-weld shot peening — critical for shoe cleat fixing performance

faq.q: What surface finishes are compatible with Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw for cycling use?
faq.a: Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw can be supplied with bead-blasted matte (Ra 1.6-3.2 µm), brushed satin, mirror polish, or PVD-colored finish. Bead-blasted + passivation is the standard for shoe cleat fixing as it provides the best balance of cosmetic consistency, corrosion resistance, and cost. Anodized colors (gold, blue, purple per ASTM B136) are available on request.

faq.a: Standard lead time for Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw is 15-25 business days depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders (3-5 working days) are available for prototype evaluation. Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw?
faq.a: Each Titanium Pedal Cleat Screw shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for shoe cleat fixing.
